implementerProof.how: I drove the same surface independently, on a local Dispatch built at 8f4a1d32 and on main e82b013b, each on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of the tester's own. Everything the proof names holds on that surface except one claim, the first-cursor fix (76d0396e). The commit message says 'a cold event stream misses nothing a relay start ... would have put below its cursor'. firstRelayCursor's comment (event_stream_relay.go:254-264) rests that on 'the delivery hub proves a horizon at boot'. The hub runs nothing until its first subscriber (delivery_live_hub.go:335, newDeliveryHub: 'Nothing runs until the first Subscribe'), and nothing else proves a horizon at boot. So on a fresh process Horizon.Proven() is 0, firstRelayCursor falls back to awaitEventCursor, and an event that commits while the first start waits never reaches the connection. The implementer's own test, TestSSEColdConnectionThatStartsTheRelayIsSentAnEventCommittedWhileItStarts, proves a horizon first with a references since read, so it does not exercise boot.

failures.criterion: Every consumer of the event stream keeps the order it relies on (the first cold connection of a process misses no event committed while the relay's first start waits; review round 5's first-cursor case, as INFRA-514's architect named it for this round).
failures.evidence: Red test e7bbbc50de53: TestSSEFirstColdConnectionOfAFreshProcessIsSentAnEventCommittedWhileTheRelayStarts in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/server_test.go. It is the implementer's test without the references read that proves a horizon first. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:16432/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run 'TestSSEFirstColdConnectionOfAFreshProcessIsSentAnEventCommittedWhileTheRelayStarts|TestSSEColdConnectionThatStartsTheRelayIsSentAnEventCommittedWhileItStarts' -count=1 -v. Result: the implementer's test PASS (6.08 s), the new one FAIL with 'server_test.go:3074: the stream sent no ... ("id: 3") within 12s'. On the real surface (adv.py firstcursor <settle>), each run used a newly started head process. A transaction in database postgres held an id; the first cold GET /api/v1/events waited; a comment POST committed id 123; then the holder committed. The stream opened 0.26 s after that and sent nothing; 123 was never delivered. The same happened with the holder taken 3 s and 10 s after /healthz. Main e82b013b sent 123 at once in all three runs. A browser loses the update: a page's first connection does not refresh on open (packages/dispatch/web/src/api/sse.ts:255-279, onOpen calls refreshEverything only when anAttemptEnded), so an event committed after the page's own reads and below the stream's first cursor never reaches that page. That last point is from reading the code; I did not drive it in a browser. Any transaction holding an id anywhere on the Cloud SQL instance at boot opens the window, and every deploy restarts the process, under D2 at one replica. Fix direction (the implementer's choice): give the relay's first start a horizon proven before the request, for example by proving one at boot, or by a cursor that cannot pass an event committing during the wait. Then correct the comment at event_stream_relay.go:259.
